newsitem.title: UK: MGAM's Smith says failings have been addressed.
newsitem.headline: MGAM's Smith says failings have been addressed.

text.p: The head of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, the fund management arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, said on Wednesday that the failings that led to a record two million pound fine from British regulators had now been addressed.
MGAM's Robert Smith said that compliance, controls and operating methods had been subjected to "rigorous review" and that he had full confidence in the people and systems now in place.

"Arrangements for the payment of compensation to investors are well advanced. Meanwhile, we continue with our primary task which is to serve our clients across the full range of the business," added Smith.

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) fined MGAM for a series of rule breaches and management failings connected with three of its funds. The funds were suspended for several days last September, after irregularities were discovered in valuations.
That discovery led to the sacking of fund manager Peter Young, who is currently under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office. Young has denied any criminal activity.

Deutsche Bank has injected 180 million pounds ($292.8 million) into the funds and has since agreed a 200 million pound compensation package with IMRO for those retail investors disadvantaged by the affair. Compensation is due to be paid by the end of the month.

IMRO said it had yet to reach its conclusions about the individuals responsible for the management and supervision of the Morgan Grenfell European Growth Trust, the Morgan Grenfell Europa Fund and the Dublin-based Morgan Grenfell European Capital Growth Fund. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
